scenario_framing: a service request that could come in at any time, organized so a person can pick it up
opportunity_headline: One way structured intake could complement the service availability your public pages already describe
opportunity_summary: Your public pages emphasize commercial HVAC repair and feature a published availability message. We built a short simulation showing how a structured intake flow could prepare a commercial request for human follow-up. We don't know your current internal process, systems, staffing, or response performance.

evidence_detail.text: a published service-availability message on the public site
commercial air-conditioning repair work ("Commercial HVAC Services")
a public request path ("Need to schedule a service call?")
a service-area reference ("Just a Sample of Our Service Areas")

unknown_summary: We don't know how your team currently handles requests, what tools, CRM or scheduling systems you use, how you're staffed, or your actual response times - none of that is public, and this simulation does not assume any of it.

simulation_input_schema.label: Service need
simulation_input_schema.exists_because: Your public pages describe commercial HVAC work, so the simulation asks which need applies.
m4_option_labels: Need to schedule a service call?
simulation_input_schema.internal_note: M4 question 'service_need': Demonstrate service-intent collection without asserting business policy. Values are synthetic demo inputs; M4 would instead derive option labels from the public evidence (recorded in m4_option_labels for audit).

simulation_input_schema.label: Facility
simulation_input_schema.exists_because: Bounded commercial facility context for the scenario.
simulation_input_schema.internal_note: M4 question 'facility_type': Demonstrate bounded commercial context collection.

simulation_input_schema.label: Service location
simulation_input_schema.exists_because: Your public pages reference a service area, so the simulation asks about location - without making any coverage promise.
m4_option_labels: Just a Sample of Our Service Areas
simulation_input_schema.internal_note: M4 question 'service_location': Route geography uncertainty to human validation; no service-area promise. Values are synthetic demo inputs; the real location is unknown, so a clearly-illustrative placeholder is used.

simulation_input_schema.label: Urgency
simulation_input_schema.exists_because: The simulation demonstrates a fixed safety handoff.
simulation_input_schema.internal_note: M4 question 'urgency': Demonstrate fixed safety handoff without emergency advice. 'Safety concern' == M4 'safety_critical' and routes to the safety exception.

simulation_input_schema.label: Equipment
simulation_input_schema.exists_because: Keeps equipment detail optional and never assumed.
simulation_input_schema.internal_note: M4 question 'equipment_context': Preserve unknown equipment details. 'Not sure' is always acceptable.

simulation_input_schema.label: Preferred follow-up
simulation_input_schema.exists_because: Chooses which preview channel the result shows; no real destination is collected.
simulation_input_schema.internal_note: M4 question 'contact_preference': Select a preview channel without collecting a destination. No real contact destination is collected - this only selects which preview channel the result shows.

result_disclosure: Nothing was sent, booked, dispatched, or updated. This was a hypothetical simulation.
closing_bridge: Imagine this fitted to your actual intake process rather than this hypothetical one.
start_over_semantics: Clears the local synthetic form state and returns to the opportunity screen so another simulation can be run. It saves nothing, sends nothing, records no history, creates no analytics, contacts no one, persists no customer data, and does not imply any real action occurred - it is a local reset only.

exception_states.title: Safety review required
exception_states.body: This simulation can't evaluate safety-critical situations. A real implementation would hand this straight to an approved human process. Nothing has been dispatched, and this screen gives no emergency advice.

exception_states.title: Outside this simulation
exception_states.body: This simulation doesn't cover that kind of request. In a real setup a person would take it from here. Nothing was sent or scheduled.

exception_states.title: Simulation hiccup
exception_states.body: The simulation couldn't finish this step. Nothing real happened - you can start over.

builder_visual_guidance: Strong product presence: deliberate typography, clearly visible selected states, a coherent visual result story, an overall polished software feel.
Opportunity framing first: lead with the opportunity, keep a calm hierarchy, keep cognitive load low.
Radical simplicity: obvious navigation and one obvious primary action per screen, easy scanning, nothing on screen that does not earn its place.
Synthesis target: premium polish, opportunity-first framing and radical simplicity together - not one at the expense of the others.
company_visual_character: No brand assets are authorized for this task. Use a premium, neutral, commercial-software presentation - restrained palette, professional typography, generous spacing. No logos, no reproduced branding, nothing implying the demo is official or affiliated.
semantics_legend: Something we actually saw on the public website. Shown as an observation and never strengthened into a promise.
Something we cannot know from public pages - your process, tools, staffing or response times. Never stated or implied.
An illustrative choice inside the simulation. Not a fact about your business and not something you told us.
An example person or role, invented to make the workflow concrete. Not real and not your staff.
Something the simulation prepared as a preview. Nothing was sent, booked, dispatched, or updated.
ux_targets: Whole flow under ~60 seconds with no instructions.
Progressive disclosure: simple first; internal detail only on request.
builder_freedom: Free: visual hierarchy, typography, colour, spacing, animation, transitions, icons, cards, responsive design, polish. Constrained: factual copy, business claims, workflow meaning, result semantics, placeholder semantics, integration state, metrics/data - use only the wording this brief supplies.
